wanted: Understand in a minute what this is and whether it is for her
did: Read the GitHub front page from the top, as a website
happened: The first paragraph is plain. Straight after it comes Status: phases, ledger sheets, GridStack, build commands. The words she needs sit among words she has never seen.
evidence: Home is widgets the sheet switches on, arranged per person, on GridStack.

wanted: Get the idea fast
did: Read the first paragraph of the README
happened: One short paragraph gave her the whole idea: her own spreadsheet, one page on top, no server, nothing to pay for.
evidence: One Google Sheet owns every number

wanted: Know if it suits a renter with one bank account and one card
did: Looked through the README and the demo page for someone like her
happened: Every example is a couple with a mortgage, an offset and a rental property. Nothing says one person renting is welcome.
evidence: A money page for one household

wanted: Know what it will cost
did: Compared the README with the Setup tab
happened: The README says nothing to pay for. Setup says $0 plus a Claude plan you already have. Nothing she read says whether a free Claude account can do this.
evidence: $0 to run. Google Sheets and a Claude plan you already have.

wanted: Know if it is safe to use with real money
did: Read the Make it yours steps in the README and on Setup
happened: Step 3 says paste your sheet into this page. Step 5 says real money needs a private copy built in Python and published by hand. Her money is real, so the path she can follow is the one she is told not to use, and the safe one she cannot do.
evidence: For real money, build with --no-snapshot and publish your own private copy.

wanted: Decide whether to trust a stranger's project with bank data
did: Looked at the repo's sidebar
happened: 0 stars, 0 forks, 2 contributors, one of them Claude. The only reason she is here is her friend.
evidence: https://github.com/EthDawg/the-kitty

wanted: Find where to start
did: Scrolled the README looking for a start here
happened: The Try it link is near the top, which is good. Make it yours is far below the file table, the data model, the month-end close and the portals. Most of the README is not for her.
evidence: https://github.com/EthDawg/the-kitty#make-it-yours

wanted: See what the thing actually is
did: Opened the Try it page
happened: It looks like a real money app within seconds: a plain verdict, a big number, things that need you. Seen in the owner's signed-in view, not a stranger's.
evidence: Worth a look.

wanted: See where the money goes
did: Opened the Insights tab
happened: A month picker and a bubble picture of spending, with a plain list beside it. This is the exact question she came with, answered for someone else's money.
evidence: Where did the money go?

wanted: Check who sees her data
did: Read the Privacy card at the bottom of Setup
happened: Short, plain, and the answer she wanted. It is the most reassuring part of the page, though it is at the very bottom.
evidence: Nothing is collected. No analytics, no tracking, no server of ours.

wanted: Start with nothing
did: Looked for a start empty control on Home, then went through Setup
happened: There is none. Home opens on the family. Make it yours sits on Setup under four long cards about how it is built, why it is built that way, and a bank list.
evidence: https://claude.ai/artifact/QH2gsDP8sHZmgMVKBtkwxn (Setup tab)

wanted: Get a blank Kitty with no fake data
did: Looked for a blank sheet in the README, on Setup and in the repo's file list
happened: The only sheet offered is a copy of the fictional family. No blank template exists in the public repo. The only way in runs through the family's data.
evidence: File → Make a copy of the demo sheet.

wanted: Remove the family from her copy
did: Read the clearing instruction against the README's own data model. Not performed.
happened: It names Transactions, Payslips and Valuations. The README says Transactions and Valuations are now formula views over Entries, and Entries, with 1,082 family rows, is not named. Public code falls back to Entries when Transactions is empty, so the family would stay on her page. Inferred from public source.
evidence: Clear the three raw tabs; fill the input tabs.

wanted: Know everything she must clear or fill
did: Read the demo sheet's tabs in read-only view and counted rows
happened: Family rows also live on tabs no step mentions: Rules 86, Contracts 20, Decisions 20, Loans 2. Accounts holds 18 rows including an SMSF, crypto and a laptop.
evidence: fill Accounts, Categories, Goals and Settings for your household

wanted: Fill in Settings as one person
did: Read the Settings tab in read-only view
happened: It is built for this couple: rows named for Jordan and Mia, income shares, work-from-home hours, rental depreciation, a refinance rate. No word on what a single renter does with them.
evidence: Jordan's share of joint income and the rental property

wanted: Make the copy
did: Stopped at the step, as the run rules require. An anonymous request to the copy link goes to Google sign-in.
happened: This needs a Google sign-in and a copy confirmation. Setup warns that a bound script comes along, with no word on what that is or what Google will say about it. Not driven.
evidence: The Kitty tab, the formulas and the bound script copy with it.

wanted: Have the setup screens make it hers
did: Read the first-visit setup screens in public source. The overlay did not appear in the owner's view.
happened: It greets a stranger with the family already loaded, then asks her name, a goal from the family's goals, a safety net against their months, and a colour. After five screens it is still their money with her name on top.
evidence: Five quick screens make it yours.

wanted: Know if this fits her hour on Sunday
did: Read the time label, then the steps under it
happened: The label says an hour. The steps include rebuilding a large sheet, a terminal script and a review file. Her hour is gone before her first file lands.
evidence: about an hour, once

wanted: Understand the name on the screen
did: Read the Home greeting
happened: The page greets Jordan and Mia, and she is Mia Davies. It feels odd for a second. This comes partly from the persona's name for this run.
evidence: Still up, Jordan and Mia

wanted: Know which version she is on
did: Read the page footer
happened: The footer says phase B while the same page explains the phase C canvas.
evidence: The Kitty 2.0 (phase B)

wanted: Find the fake bank
did: Opened the portals landing page
happened: Clear, funny and honest about being a demo. She smiles. It makes the project feel made by a person.
evidence: The bank that lands on its feet.

wanted: Sign in without worrying
did: Read the Westpaw sign-in page
happened: The demo note also teaches her something true about real banks. A nice touch.
evidence: A real portal would never say that

wanted: See her one everyday account and export it
did: Read the portal's public code and the repo's screenshots. Sign-in was not driven.
happened: Any name opens the same family. Westpaw shows five accounts including a home loan and a rental, not one everyday account. There is no way to be a different household here, so her bank files are the family's files too.
evidence: https://github.com/EthDawg/the-kitty/blob/main/docs/screenshots/portals/westpaw-activity.png

wanted: Put her exported file somewhere so the page can use it
did: Read what the portal says after a download, then searched the page's public code for any way to add a file
happened: The portal tells her to save into a folder she does not have and run a program she has never heard of. The page has no file upload. Drive plays no part. Her data can only land through a Python script in a copy of the repo on a laptop. This is where the path ends for her.
evidence: Save it, unchanged, under sources/<account>/<today>/ and run the importer.

wanted: Enter her bank on the Accounts tab
did: Read the importer's public source. Not run.
happened: One bank has three names: the real bank it parodies, Westpaw, Harbour Bank. The importer accepts only Harbour Bank, Southern Card, Wattle Credit Union or Bark Bank. If she types the name of her bank it stops. No step tells her to type a fictional bank's name instead.
evidence: which has no adapter

wanted: Know what account means in the folder path
did: Read the skill and the portal message
happened: The folder must be the id from the Accounts tab, such as ACC-EVD. The portal hands her Data.csv and activity.csv and calls it account. The link is only spelled out in the agent skill.
evidence: Every folder name is an id from the Accounts tab

wanted: Have her first month add up
did: Read portals/README.md
happened: Each account needs its balance from the day before the first file, or the import holds. That rule is only in the portals README, not in Make it yours.
evidence: at its balance the day before the first file

wanted: Get last month's card spending
did: Read the Amewx path in public data
happened: Card statements close on the 14th, so a statement is not last month. She has to know to pick a calendar month rather than the statement, which is what she would reach for.
evidence: Statement periods close on the 14th and straddle two months

wanted: Follow the export steps for a real bank
did: Read the bank list on Setup
happened: The bank entries shown carry a stamp saying nobody has checked them on the bank's site. Honest, and it lowers her confidence.
evidence: not yet verified in a browser

wanted: Read the sign-in form
did: Read the page's text straight after it loaded
happened: The form was not there for the first moment. It appeared a few seconds later, after a 401 came back. An agent reading fast sees an empty page.
evidence: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401

wanted: Not see a broken page when her sheet is empty
did: Read the page's public code for the empty state. Not reached live.
happened: The empty sheet message is warm and plain. Its button leads back to the same importer step.
evidence: Your sheet is set up. It just has no transactions yet.

wanted: See her one account described properly
did: Read the Home code for one account. Inferred, not seen.
happened: The big number would be labelled cash and offset across 1 accounts. Wrong plural, and offset means nothing to a renter.
evidence: cash and offset across

wanted: See a useful page from one month of data
did: Read the Home and Insights code and searched it for any wording about having little data. Inferred, not seen.
happened: Home would show a 12-month card with one bar, a 3-month savings rate and a safety net worked out from one month. No wording for a first month turned up.
evidence: The last 12 months

wanted: Find proof that a very small household has been looked at
did: Read the fixtures in the public repo
happened: The smallest fixture is six cash accounts and every transaction. No public fixture or screenshot shows one account and one month.
evidence: the six cash accounts and every transaction

wanted: Find the instructions for setting up a new household
did: Looked for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and llms.txt, read the file tree, read the only skill
happened: Those three files do not exist. The one skill covers the monthly close and assumes a working sheet with accounts on it. Nothing tells an agent how to start a household from nothing.
evidence: for each account on the sheet's Accounts tab

wanted: Do it for Mia with what she has, which is Claude with Drive and Sheets
did: Read the skill's stated runtimes and the steps it needs
happened: The skill names Claude Code and Codex. It needs the repo on disk, Python and a browser. No step says how to install it. An agent holding only her connectors cannot run the importer as written.
evidence: Works for Claude Code (built-in browser or Claude in Chrome

wanted: Give the importer a snapshot of Mia's sheet
did: Read snapshot.py and tools/grid_to_snapshot.py
happened: The importer plans from a saved snapshot. snapshot.py needs the sheet's script published to anyone, plus a public feed setting real households are told to leave off. The other tool carries tabs over from a base file and refuses when Transactions differ, and her only base is the family. An agent would have to invent the file by hand.
evidence: a household with real money leaves it off

wanted: Land the rows correctly
did: Compared the README and Setup with the skill
happened: README and Setup say append. The skill forbids appending and requires a plan, explicit ranges and a verified re-read. The README's example command also leaves out the flag the skill uses for the ledger sheet.
evidence: Never `append_values`, never a range the plan does not name

wanted: Run the importer for Mia without touching the family
did: Read the importer's defaults
happened: By default it reads the family's snapshot, looks in a sources folder full of the family's files, and takes the sheet id from the snapshot or the project's config. An agent has to know to override all of it.
evidence: default: the snapshot's, else kitty.config.json

wanted: Follow the private copy path
did: Compared the Setup instruction with the repo's file list
happened: Setup points at a kitty folder that is not in the public repo. build.py is at the top level. The publish step also needs a capability list that only the README gives.
evidence: python3 kitty/build.py --no-snapshot

wanted: List what the public instructions leave open
did: Wrote down each guess needed to do this for Mia
happened: Which tabs are formulas and must stay; which rows to clear; which of the Davies categories suit a renter; what to do with the couple's Settings rows; whether Drive can make the copy with its script; which plan is needed; how to get CSV into a sheet from chat. The docs only say to use the template.
evidence: A household with different tab names or columns needs the sheet template

wanted: Sign in to the portals for Mia
did: Stopped at the form. This agent's rules bar typing a password on a site that is not local or named as a test environment, even a public demo one.
happened: The agent cannot finish this step alone, and the project's own rule agrees: the person signs in. Mia has to do it herself. Nothing behind the form was seen live.
evidence: You never see, type, read or store a password

wanted: Know the rules of the job
did: Read the skill and the importer's notes
happened: Clear, firm rules, no credentials ever, and an importer written to stop and say exactly what is wrong. For the monthly close, an agent is in safe hands.
evidence: names the file, the row and what to do
